candidates.exact_span: EPA used the San Juan River geometric mean hardness of 132 mg/l (expressed as CaCO3) provided by NMED.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If the hardness value used to derive or select pollutant-specific limits is interpreted differently (e.g., wrong receiving-water hardness, unit, or averaging basis), the applicable numeric cyanide or other hardness-dependent limits for compliance comparison could change.

candidates.exact_span: the draft permit will propose a daily maximum and monthly average limits of 22 ug/L and 14.67 ug/L, respectively, for Cyanide.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of whether these proposed limits are the operative enforceable limits (versus illustrative draft language) would change which numeric thresholds are used to evaluate reported cyanide measurements.

candidates.exact_span: The facility shall have a 1-year compliance schedule to achieve final limitations for Cyanide pollutant.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether FY2025 falls inside the compliance-schedule period and whether interim versus final cyanide limits apply during that period would change limit-applicability determinations (A) and how missing or interim-period results are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: Technology based pollutants; BOD5 and TSS, are proposed to be monitored five times per week, with sampling on at least five different days.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the required sampling frequency and day-distribution rule affects whether reported BOD5/TSS data satisfy the applicable monitoring obligation for each period in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Flow is proposed to be monitored continuously using a totalizing meter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: If continuous totalizing-meter monitoring is the operative requirement, adequacy of flow evidence and expected data density differ from periodic grab/composite sampling, changing whether monitoring was required and whether gaps constitute missing required evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Sample type for BOD5 and TSS is 12-Hr composite.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different interpretation of required sample type (composite duration/method) could reclassify reported measurements as non-compliant with monitoring requirements even when numeric results exist.

candidates.exact_span: The monitoring frequencies of daily for TRC and five times per week for E. coli, pH and flow are consistent with the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage states flow is monitored five times per week while another sentence in the same segment proposes continuous flow monitoring; resolving that tension changes which flow-monitoring obligation is treated as applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Report requirements of once per week for TDS is also consistent with the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TDS is a report-only requirement versus a compliance-limit monitoring obligation affects whether numeric limit comparison applies (A) and how absent TDS results are categorized (C).

candidates.exact_span: The draft permit will not propose any WET limits. However, continuation of WET monitoring is proposed in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Absence of numeric WET limits changes whether WET results trigger limit-exceedance analysis (A), while continued monitoring still imposes reporting obligations whose applicability must be evaluated (B) and whose non-numeric or missing outcomes require missing-evidence classification (C).

candidates.exact_span: When the critical dilution is equal to or less than 10%, in lieu of the 7-day chronic test, a 48-hour acute test may be run using a 10:1 acute to chronic ratio; 23.4% rounded to the nearest whole number 23%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the facility critical dilution (stated as 2.34% elsewhere in the segment), the ≤10% substitution rule, and the rounding convention determines whether acute versus chronic WET testing was required.

candidates.exact_span: The facility shall conduct a 48-hour acute test using Daphnia pulex once per quarter, and a 48-hour acute test using Pimephales promelas once per quarter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of species, test type, and quarterly frequency would change which WET monitoring events are counted as required in each FY2025 quarter.

candidates.exact_span: After the first four quarters without failures, the permittee may apply for a frequency reduction.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the four-quarter failure-free condition is met and whether an approved frequency reduction is in effect changes the monitoring frequency treated as applicable in later FY2025 quarters.

candidates.exact_span: Any failure afterwards shall re-establish all tests for both species to once per quarter for the remainder of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of what constitutes a WET failure and when it occurred determines whether quarterly testing obligations were re-triggered for the remainder of the permit term, including FY2025 periods.

candidates.exact_span: The test series will be 10%, 13%, 17%, 23% and 31%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The required dilution series governs whether submitted WET tests match the prescribed protocol (B) and whether nonstandard or missing dilution results should be treated as inadequate evidence rather than ordinary numeric compliance outcomes (C).
